agent_runs.notes: Updated `model.fr` in place: renamed the custom hypercolor index from `HC` to `HCIndex` to avoid colliding with FeynRules’ `HC[...]`, removed redundant neutral `Q -> 0` quantum-number declarations from self-conjugate fields, replaced the final nonstandard `LVLCNP` assignment with the required final `LTot := ...`, excluded the expensive full `MatrixExp` chiral term from `LTot` to avoid the compile timeout while keeping the explicit expanded terms, added explicit normalized composite-scalar kinetic terms plus the missing `etaP` mass term, and converted the unsummed expanded pion/K interaction into explicit finite `Sum[...]` expressions. I could not run the full Wolfram/FeynRules validation locally because `wolframscript` is present but has no configured WolframKernel.

Updated `model.fr` in place by replacing raw `Phi`/`Phibar` Higgs-doublet references with explicit SM component aliases `PhiSM`/`PhiSMBar`, including in `Mmat`, `LUVVLC`, `LMExpanded`, and `LEDM`, so UFO generation should no longer emit malformed `Phi/Phibar` particles. I also rewrote `LUVVLC` in component form for `L0`, `Lm`, and `Nvlc`, and symmetrized the fermion kinetic term as `1/2 (kin + HC[kin])` to remove the hermiticity-check failure from the gauge-current terms without changing the physical content. `LTot` remains the final top-level assignment. Full validation could not be run here because `wolframscript` has no configured WolframKernel.

Updated `model.fr` in place by adding physical-basis electroweak helpers for `Wi` and `B` (`WiPhys`, `BPhys`, and corresponding field strengths), then rewrote the triplet kinetic gauge interaction and anomaly terms to use `W`, `Wbar`, `Z`, and `A` instead of raw `Wi`/`B` gauge-eigenstate objects; I also updated the inactive `LEDM` helper consistently. This targets the reported MadGraph failure where UFO export tried to create an invalid `Wi` particle entry, while preserving the same operator structure and leaving `LTot` as the final top-level assignment. I could not rerun the full tool chain here because `wolframscript` cannot locate a configured `WolframKernel`.
